title: Pointwise left derived mixed tensor

from.place: proof of Tag 0DJ8: choose K-flat models for the derived tensor over R; Tag 06Y6 construction of the fixed-second-factor derived tensor

statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings, $f:R\to A$ a ring homomorphism, and $N$ an unbounded cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write $Q_R,Q_A$ for the localization functors to $D(R),D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $B_N(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)$ for the mixed total tensor [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor]. There exist a functor $L:D(R)\to D(A)$ and a natural transformation $\varepsilon:Q_R L\to B_N Q_A$ such that $(L,\varepsilon)$ is a left derived functor of $B_N Q_A$ with respect to quasi-isomorphisms, $L$ admits a shift compatibility making it triangulated, and $\varepsilon_F$ is an isomorphism for every ordinary-module K-flat complex $F$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

proof.text: The mixed module bifunctor is additive in each variable: extension of scalars is additive by its adjunction, and tensor is additive. Its induced functor on homotopy categories has the shift and mapping-cone compatibilities provided by the existing bifunctor machinery. Composing with Qh_A gives an exact functor Fh:K(R) → D(A).

Use the source library ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution and the reduced resolution functor. Its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, and kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj proves its source K-flat. After the homotopy quotient this gives the resolution hypothesis for the K-flat class P. Lift homotopy maps to complex maps using fullness of the quotient. The first clause of lem-pc-mixed-tensor-kflat-quasi-iso gives the inversion hypothesis.

Apply leftDerived_from_resolvingClass to Fh and P. It yields L, a counit on K(R), triangulatedness, and invertibility of the counit on P. Whisker by the homotopy quotient and transport with quotientCompQhIso and quotientCompBifunctorMapHomotopyFlipObjIso to obtain epsilon on complexes. Its K-flat components are isomorphisms by composition.

The existing K-flat left derivability structure on complexes applies. The theorem LocalizerMorphism.isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivabilityStructure proves the right Kan universal property from invertibility of epsilon on K-flat objects. This proves the left-derived property along Q_R without any additional selection of data.

lean.statement: theorem exists_mixedTensor_pointwise_leftDerived {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{wR} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] (f : R →+* A) (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) : let B := (ModuleCat.mixedTensor f).flip.map₂CochainComplex ∃ (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (ε : (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ ⥤ _) ⋙ L ⟶ B.flip.obj N ⋙ (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat A) ℤ ⥤ _)), L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat R) (.up ℤ)) ∧ (∃ c : L.CommShift ℤ, letI := c; L.IsTriangulated) ∧ (∀ F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ, (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat R) (.up ℤ)).kFlat F → IsIso (ε.app F))
